minutes.headline: Select Board kept a single tax rate with no exemptions and approved three Verizon conduit petitions.
minutes.summary: The board backed a DLTA request to update the housing production plan, approved three Verizon conduit petitions after a public hearing, and held the tax classification hearing, choosing a single rate. The town manager gave her report and a mid-year review of FY27 goals, including FY28 budget planning. The board discussed special town meeting follow-up and went into executive session on the food pantry license.

what_happened.line: After a public hearing, the Select Board voted unanimously to keep a single tax rate, with no open space discount and no residential or small commercial exemption.
The board unanimously approved the Williams Drive, Country Road and Chase Road Verizon conduit petitions as presented.
The board voted unanimously to support a DLTA request for a housing production plan update and authorized the planning director to sign the cover letter.
Special town meeting follow-up ended without a resolution; Brooks House RFP next steps and a TCP decision are to be taken up.
FY28 budget priorities and service levels are tentatively set for December 8th, and the December 1st meeting is cancelled.

why_it_matters: The single-rate vote means homes and businesses stay on the same rate. A split rate was discussed as saving a small amount per home while raising the average business bill by much more.
The FY28 budget discussion and the school committee's first draft, which cites rising costs and restoring four elementary teachers, will shape next year's tax bills and service levels.
